clue.text: Drunken priests initially botching hymn during services

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word botching only
during puts the hymn in the middle of the services, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: aces are services in tennis, serves that win the point outright
a chant is a sung hymn or psalm

explanation.surface: Tipsy clergy start mangling the hymn in the middle of church services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Services' looks ecclesiastical, but here it is tennis: ACES are unreturned serves.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchantes were the frenzied, wine-fuelled devotees and priestesses of the god Bacchus.

clue.text: Trouble for rambler, say, where many accidents occur

definitions.meaning: a rambler is a climbing rose, and this fungal disease mars rose leaves
a road location notorious for crashes

explanation.walkthrough: 'rambler' suggests a hiker, but it is a rambling rose.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose disease and the accident hotspot share one name.

clue.text: Official sporting nothing in button hole?

indicators.note: sporting means wearing, so the outer word carries the zero within it

parts.note: to buttonhole someone is to corner them
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A dignitary has nothing in their buttonhole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'button hole' suggests a flower in a lapel; it is the verb buttonhole, to corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner is a public official who investigates sudden deaths.

clue.text: Heading out of Valencia, taking time to BIL travel to another Spanish resort

indicators.note: to travel is to move about, so these letters are rearranged
heading out of means the first letter leaves the city name

explanation.surface: A tourist leaves Valencia and takes time to go to another Spanish holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove V, the first letter, from VALENCIA, add T, and rearrange ALENCIAT; 'travel' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a Spanish Mediterranean resort, down the coast from Valencia.

clue.text: Literary work puts forward idea about tabloid topless girls

annotationWithheld.why: Literary work puts forward idea about tabloid topless girls: THE SUN and (G)ALS are clear, but no reading of 'puts forward idea about' gives the remaining letters; the clue appears garbled in the held text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Literary work puts forward idea about tabloid topless girls

clue.text: Notes made by instrument on the Titanic, perhaps

indicators.note: on here means aboard, so the instrument is inside the ship

parts.note: SS, steamship, prefixes ship names like the Titanic
the harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Music played by the band aboard the doomed liner.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharps are notes raised a semitone in music.

clue.text: First signs of cloudy and misty period affected holiday location

indicators.note: first signs of means the opening letters of each of the following four words

explanation.surface: A gloomy, misty spell spoilt the holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' joins the wordplay to the definition here, as in 'acted on', though camp also means affected in manner, a bonus second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp is a place where holidaymakers stay, as in a holiday camp or campsite.

clue.text: Diver runs into lake with a loud shout

indicators.note: into means the runs letter goes inside the lake's name

parts.note: Como is an Italian lake
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a rant is a loud tirade

explanation.surface: A swimmer charges into the lake yelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The cormorant is a seabird that dives underwater for fish.

clue.text: See large bird peck old man of Jordan

parts.note: the moa was a huge extinct flightless bird of New Zealand
a peck is a small bite

explanation.surface: Watch a big bird nip an elderly Jordanian.
explanation.definitionFit: A Moabite was an inhabitant of ancient Moab, in present-day Jordan.

clue.text: Is a brave sort, though irritating

indicators.note: to sort is to put in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone courageous can still be grating company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' reads as a noun (a brave sort of person) but is the verb signalling the rearrangement of IS A BRAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive manners are harsh and grating, so the word is a synonym for irritating.

clue.text: Female abandons part of course, needing breathing space

indicators.note: abandons means the female letter leaves the longer word

parts.note: the fairway is the mown part of a golf course

explanation.surface: A woman golfer walks off the fairway, needing room to breathe.
explanation.definitionFit: An airway is the passage that carries air to the lungs, literally a space for breathing.

clue.text: Philosopher king, social type

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
ants are classic social insects, living in organised colonies

explanation.surface: A monarch who is both thinker and party animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social type' suggests a gregarious person; it is a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanuel Kant was the eighteenth-century German philosopher of the Critique of Pure Reason.

clue.text: Deep fear?

parts.note: reads as a profound dread, but the deep is the sea, so this is a dread of water

explanation.definitionFit: Hydrophobia's Latin-rooted twin names a morbid dread of water, and the deep is a name for the sea.

clue.text: Dicky, Peter and Paul going on and on?

indicators.note: dicky means unsound or shaky, so the names are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two apostles with weak hearts keep rambling endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a third name beside Peter and Paul; it is the adjective meaning faulty, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perpetual continues without end, so it is forever going on.

clue.text: Gold coin (sovereign) for armed sol

annotationWithheld.why: Gold coin (sovereign) for armed sol: PISTOLE plus ER is clear, but the definition 'armed sol' is cut short in the held text and no source restores it.

clue.text: I'll get ready — OK to enter gym?

indicators.note: to enter means one word goes inside the other

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
aye is an affirmative, yes or okay

explanation.surface: Someone preparing to go into the gym asks whether that is allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is slang for cash (the readies), so the definition is the one who receives the money.
explanation.definitionFit: The person being paid is the one who will receive the readies, British slang for cash.

clue.text: Socially confident sort, no longer on the wagon, embraces party animal

parts.note: ex means former, no longer

indicators.note: embraces means one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means abstaining from drink
a raver is a keen partygoer

explanation.surface: A gregarious type has fallen off the wagon and hugs a partygoer.
explanation.definitionFit: An extravert, the older spelling of extrovert, is outgoing and confident in company.

clue.text: Citrus fruit in a lemon squash

indicators.note: to squash is to crush out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lemon goes into a fruit drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squash' looks like the British fruit cordial; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The minneola is a tangelo, a citrus hybrid of tangerine and grapefruit.

clue.text: Deal card face upwards, and cheat

definitions.meaning: in pontoon a player who says this asks for a card dealt face up

explanation.surface: A card sharp deals one face up and then swindles the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is the British name for the card game blackjack.
explanation.definitionFit: The card-game call and the verb for swindling share one word.

clue.text: One with hopes of arrest in decline

indicators.note: in means the arrest word sits within the decline word

parts.note: to wane is to decline
to nab is to arrest

explanation.surface: Someone hopeful of an arrest finds his career on the slide.
explanation.definitionFit: A wannabe is an aspirant who hopes to become someone admired.

clue.text: Dunce is hit hard by start of term: help!

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: start of means the opening letter of the word term

explanation.surface: A dim pupil is badly shaken by the new term and cries out.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark turns 'help!' into a cry; the definition is the noun, a helper.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant is a helper, someone who gives aid.

clue.text: Campaign to have a barrier put round it

indicators.note: put round means the barrier encloses the word it

parts.note: a gate is a barrier

explanation.surface: Protesters demand a fence be erected around a site.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to campaign actively for a cause.

clue.text: King partly suffered raw deal, being overthrown

indicators.note: overthrown means turned over, so the letters read backwards
partly means the letters come from part of the phrase

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch got a bad deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'suffered raw deal' lies DRAWDE, which reads backwards as the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward is the name of several English kings.

clue.text: No particular heavy metal song

definitions.meaning: scrap ferrous metal of whatever sort, as a rag-and-bone man calls it
a famous British music-hall comic song

explanation.surface: Any heavy metal track will do.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag-and-bone men collected scrap from British streets; 'heavy metal song' suggests a rock genre.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means scrap of whatever kind and is also the title of a music-hall number.

clue.text: Walk with difficulty, not quite reaching a distant city

indicators.note: not quite reaching means the last letter is missing

parts.note: to limp is to walk unevenly

explanation.surface: Hobbling, the traveller doesn't quite make it to a far-off city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima, capital of Peru, is a far-flung city from a British setter's view.

clue.text: One never lies about onset of middle age

parts.note: ca, circa, is Latin for about

indicators.note: onset of means the first letter of the word middle

parts.note: an era is an age

explanation.surface: Someone claims total honesty about reaching middle age.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'the camera never lies' supplies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that photographs record truthfully, so this device is the one that never lies.

clue.text: Succeeded getting head servant on strike

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
the top is the head of something
a page is a boy servant

explanation.surface: A head servant takes over just as the staff walk out.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a halt to work, an industrial strike.

clue.text: River sport

definitions.meaning: the ... flows through Durham in north-east England
to sport a garment is to have it on

explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' looks like a noun (a game) but is the verb, as in sporting a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The English river shares its name with the verb for having clothes on.

clue.text: Being struck off has local employees in distress? Not half

indicators.note: in means the bar staff sit inside the shortened word
not half means only the first half of distress is used

parts.note: a local is a pub, whose employees are barmen

explanation.surface: A pub's staff are upset at losing their licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is British for one's neighbourhood pub. 'Not half' also reads as slang for 'very much'.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbarment is expulsion from the bar, a lawyer being struck off.
